title: The BEST Game you've never heard of - Polygon
description:
Polygon: An INCREDIBLE free-to-play Battlefield-like on Steam!

0:00 Intro
0:18 Gameplay
6:27 Game-modes
7:33 Maps
10:45 Developer(s)

asr.full_text: This is Polygon. I discovered this Gen recently and have been hooked ever since. But you might not have even ever heard of it. I´ve personally seen zero marketing for this game, which is a shame. And I am going to show you the best this game has to offer, and why it´s worth checking out this Free2Play shooter yourself. Let´s jump straight to the most important thing in my opinion. The Gameplay. Is it fun and is it well designed? The answer to both of these questions is a resounding YES. Polygon is fast pace arcade-y style shooter with a few realism slash milson elements thrown in. Polygon plays like other games within the vein of a BatlleField style. Think BattleBit, Delta Force and, of course, the namesake Battlefield. Your movement heavily relies upon this stamina bar, which is used for sprinting and jumping. You do have a decent amount of stamina to start with, but it is slow to regenerate. This leads to thoughtful player choice and skill in managing this resource. You can't just sprint around with no penalty, you need to pick your moments. Be mindful of when you are low stamina and make quick dashes from cover to cover. The other realism, slash milsim element, comes into the movement itself. It's rugged, robust and intentional. And it feels good. How you move in a gunfight can make a difference. Rapidly changing directions adds wobble and sway to your gun so you need to make split-second decisions on whether to hold an angle, long strafe or try to go back and forth. Reload The next element to keep in mind is reload. Reloads are long enough that you need cover to stay safe, but not needlessly long slowing the gameplay down. And swapping to your pistol is actually useful. Switch to your pistol Also, isn't this cool? When you swap to your pistol, if you look down, you see that your primary is holstered on a sling on the Gameplay elements in Polygon are so well designed, it creates thoughtful, meaningful, moment to moment gameplay where decisions are important. Restrictions breed creativity, and mastering Polygon is rewarding. It's good to compare this to modern shooters like Call of Duty, Battlefield, Apex legends, etc. as those games kind of let you turn your brain off and autopilot run around. Basically, infinite statminar bars and reloads that are fast and save their progress. Polygon rewards players for paying attention and actively engages your brain. I've covered movement, reloading, how's the shooting? It's great! Guns are snappy, recoil is meaningful but not overtop, muzzle velocity is fast but you still need to give a slight target lead at a distance. Visibility while shooting is good and the tracers offer feedback to adjust your shot. No dispersion to be seen when aiming down sight. You aren't actively fighting malfunctioning barrel guns. Each gun's sound is unique and actually, shooting makes a decently audible sound for those around you, but is inaudible at a long enough range. Firing willy nilly gives away your position, accompanied with bright muzzle flashes around you. This also means if you choose to take a sniper or DMR and have enough distance, the target won't even be aware you're shooting them until they get hit. How you position when you choose to shoot, and how to reposition are so important. The time to kill is very rapid. Players have 100 health or 60 in hardcore servers and guns do 20-40 damage per shot, so each gun kills in between 0.1 and 0.3 seconds. Polygon only has 15 weapons, 12 primaries and three secondaries. I'll explain why so few later, but for now, there isn't any bloat. The weapons all offer significant differences and finding the one you mesh well with gives reason to explore new weapons. The weapon balance is pretty spot on. All the guns are powerful and worth using with their own trade-offs. You won't find a SMG-1 and then a basically identical clone SMG-2 with 0.5 less damage and 1% faster ADS speed. One criticism I do have for the game, however, is the attachment system. I do like that it's actually more minimal, adding gadgets and extensions to the weapon, rather than completely CUrsifying them, like the COD Weaponsmith. My issue with the system is that It's clearly Adding gadgets and extensions to the weapon, rather than completely cursing the weapon like the Cob weaponsmith. My issue with this system is that it's clearly still more of a placeholder than what I think is planned for the future, when it's revisited and fleshed out. Each weapon can take an optic, a barrel attachment, and some can take a foregrip and flashlight. The problem is that the positives and negatives from the attachments are less than 10% boosts in either direction. The optimal setup on basically every gun is a vertical foregrip with the Hunter Style Muzzle Break reducing as much recoil as possible from each weapon while only sacrificing a tiny bit of aiming & swapping speed both of which are negligible compared to the improved recoil. All of the other attachments options are really weak and there isn't any room for experimenting other than finding out that the rest of the attachments are… The choices of optics are pretty good though. Each player will have a preference for Sight picture and magnification level. The loadout you spawn with is pretty simple. Any Primary and Secondary can be equipped together. Each player spawns with two grenades and plenty of ammo. These can be refilled at ammo and health stations around the map, usually near objectives. I would again criticize the game here a bit, as there are no restrictions on the number of snipers per team, and since everyone can have the same guns and looks the same, it can sometimes be hard to tell if the person you're looking at is a friendly or enemy , there isn't any friendly fire, so you can just do a shot-check in case, but if there's an enemy in front of you and some allies in the distance, or behind a wall, directly behind them, it can lead to confusion getting you killed. Also, in these kind of games, the quality of a match decreases as the number of recon or sniper players increases. Having people jerking off to the back of the map and not making any action about the objective leads to more boring games, with less hype, and if a team is overloaded with snipers, a boring stomp as one team gets stuck in a base spawn. Lastly for gameplay, Polygon is focused on one game mode, conquest. There is always objectives on the map to be captured and controlled, keeping the action flowing. Maps will have between 1 to 3 control points , that generate the team that owns its score. The only way for a team to win is by holding the objectives – your kills and deaths don't matter. Capturing an objective also grants your team some map control, as now you can spawn to the location rather than just your HQ. A nice thing the game does is actually updating your spawn point on the respawn screen to the closest one near your last death, so you can quickly get back into the action in that area without having to think about it. There is a second game mode available on a few maps called King of the Hill where both teams fight to control a single objective that doesn't move usually located in the centre of the map. This mode adjusts the focal points of the maps and makes them play out differently than in Conquest. Sometimes in games I feel like the maps play the same even with different objectives but Polygon nails are here The two modes are well designed and fun to play But we can't discuss game modes in full detail without looking in the maps of they are played on right listen polygon has got some of the Hands-down Best maps in a shooter for a long time each map is unique offers different gameplay opportunities and is refined and crafted to perfection. You can just feel the amount of care that has been poured into each location and each sight line. Different positions on the map give power in some way but a counterable weakness in another. Cover and foliage are placed to allow you to make a quick route through the map, allowing for aggressive and proactive plays to be made, which is way more exciting than being caged in a box, playing slow from the back of the map. Flanking routes allow you to safely get closer to key areas, making breakthroughs and comebacks as you try different avenues of attack. Leading the charge or supporting from a crossfire position, holding ground to make space for your team or going for the long play flank.. There is always options and no match is truly stagnant. We've got the classic Valley although this is biased as I played my first handful of games on it. A fantastic three capture map with a high ground position, a scrappy middle ground fight within trees and boulders, and a rundown motel where you can get shot from any window. You've got Sandstorm, an Egypt-themed map centred around a downed Blackhawk. With nooks and crannies to be careful of, as well as paranoia from the dozens of windows, balconies and rooftops that enemies can appear from. You've got to stay moving. Agile. If you slow down and reveal your position, you could die at any time. It's frenetic. AND THEN, the maps namesake, a sandstorm erupts and vision is obscured. Those long-range positions are no longer as favourable and you can close-in and dig out pesky campers. The pace is broken up and it's as exhilarating as it is difficult to survive here. You've also got Metro. C'mon, you know what this is! Winding side passages and long sightlines has teams battling back and forth for lines of control. We've also got cargo! You surely know what this is! I joke, but these two maps do offer refinement, but keep the essence of what they are inspired from. Crash Site takes us to a military base on a small island where a large carrier plane has crashed. This map creates choke points using long fences that teams control and fight over. Staying aware and holding down the sightlines slows down the enemy team and create space for your team to escape the spawns. Uniquely, there is a fair amount of building-to-building combat, and there's always an annoying fucka up here in this goddamn ruff. Finally, we have Storage. Personally, I'll criticise this map as I think it's a little unfair towards the team spawning here. It's really difficult to get out of this spawn. map as I think it's a little unfair towards team-spawn. Other than that, I do enjoy fighting around massive refinery silos and inside warehouses. There are safer ways to get through the map with, or risk taking the wrap- up the long drainage canals. So, I want to circle back to a point I made earlier. FIFA guns, two modes, six maps. It doesn't sound like a lot of content. Sure, the quality is definitely there, and most things aren't left unfinished and have clearly has a lot of work put in based on feedback and testing. The reason why there isn't more content, other than that it's well polished is that Polygon is made entirely by one developer. Knod or Nick has built Polygon over the course of years, refining their craft, expanding their skill set and perfecting this game. Polygon initially released in early 2020 Access and has come a long way. I was a little disappointed to find, however, that the main focus for Nod has become working on Polygon too. This sequel to the game is rebuilt entirely from the ground up, with the intention of adding vehicles, larger-scale maps, destruction physics and soldier classes. You can read the history of the game's development for yourself on the RE-DASTA'S Studios patreon, where it mentions a heavy inspiration from Battlefield 3 and 4. And you can definitely see it. Don't worry though! Polygon 1 is still worth playing on its own merits and as second developer and community manager, Wolf has joined re joined Redasta Studios to bring updates and refinements to Polygon 1. I am super excited to see the bright future these devs and games have. Please, please, keep in mind, I am in no way affiliated or sponsored by Redasta Studio. I just really love this game and was stoked to share it with you. Polygon is free to play on Steam, and hopefully I've convinced you to try it out. Thanks so much for watching, and I'll see you on the Polycool. Polyester... Polymer? Polyoxyl Benzyl Methylengli-Colonhidride-Polygon! To be honest, the name could do with a bit of rebranding, or something to make it easier to find online...

Polygon: An INCREDIBLE free-to-play Battlefield-like on Steam! 0:00 Intro 0:18 Gameplay 6:27 Game-modes 7:33 Maps 10:45 Developer(s)

This is Polygon. I discovered this Gen recently and have been hooked ever since. But you might not have even ever heard of it. I´ve personally seen zero marketing for this game, which is a shame. And I am going to show you the best this game has to offer, and why it´s worth checking out this Free2Play shooter yourself. Let´s jump straight to the most important thing in my opinion. The Gameplay. Is it fun and is it well designed? The answer to both of these questions is a resounding YES. Polygon is fast pace arcade-y style shooter with a few realism slash milson elements thrown in. Polygon plays like other games within the vein of a BatlleField style. Think BattleBit, Delta Force and, of course, the namesake Battlefield. Your movement heavily relies upon this stamina bar, which is used for sprinting and jumping. You do have a decent amount of stamina to start with, but it is slow to regenerate. This leads to thoughtful player choice and skill in managing this resource. You can't just sprint around with no penalty, you need to pick your moments. Be mindful of when you are low stamina and make quick dashes from cover to cover. The other realism, slash milsim element, comes into the movement itself. It's rugged, robust and intentional. And it feels good. How you move in a gunfight can make a difference. Rapidly changing directions adds wobble and sway to your gun so you need to make split-second decisions on whether to hold an angle, long strafe or try to go back and forth. Reload The next element to keep in mind is reload. Reloads are long enough that you need cover to stay

safe, but not needlessly long slowing the gameplay down. And swapping to your pistol is actually useful. Switch to your pistol Also, isn't this cool? When you swap to your pistol, if you look down, you see that your primary is holstered on a sling on the Gameplay elements in Polygon are so well designed, it creates thoughtful, meaningful, moment to moment gameplay where decisions are important. Restrictions breed creativity, and mastering Polygon is rewarding. It's good to compare this to modern shooters like Call of Duty, Battlefield, Apex legends, etc. as those games kind of let you turn your brain off and autopilot run around. Basically, infinite statminar bars and reloads that are fast and save their progress. Polygon rewards players for paying attention and actively engages your brain. I've covered movement, reloading, how's the shooting? It's great! Guns are snappy, recoil is meaningful but not overtop, muzzle velocity is fast but you still need to give a slight target lead at a distance. Visibility while shooting is good and the tracers offer feedback to adjust your shot. No dispersion to be seen when aiming down sight. You aren't actively fighting malfunctioning barrel guns. Each gun's sound is unique and actually, shooting makes a decently audible sound for those around you, but is inaudible at a long enough range. Firing willy nilly gives away your position, accompanied with bright muzzle flashes around you. This also means if you choose to take a sniper or DMR and have enough distance, the target won't even be aware you're shooting them until they get hit. How

you position when you choose to shoot, and how to reposition are so important. The time to kill is very rapid. Players have 100 health or 60 in hardcore servers and guns do 20-40 damage per shot, so each gun kills in between 0.1 and 0.3 seconds. Polygon only has 15 weapons, 12 primaries and three secondaries. I'll explain why so few later, but for now, there isn't any bloat. The weapons all offer significant differences and finding the one you mesh well with gives reason to explore new weapons. The weapon balance is pretty spot on. All the guns are powerful and worth using with their own trade-offs. You won't find a SMG-1 and then a basically identical clone SMG-2 with 0.5 less damage and 1% faster ADS speed. One criticism I do have for the game, however, is the attachment system. I do like that it's actually more minimal, adding gadgets and extensions to the weapon, rather than completely CUrsifying them, like the COD Weaponsmith. My issue with the system is that It's clearly Adding gadgets and extensions to the weapon, rather than completely cursing the weapon like the Cob weaponsmith. My issue with this system is that it's clearly still more of a placeholder than what I think is planned for the future, when it's revisited and fleshed out. Each weapon can take an optic, a barrel attachment, and some can take a foregrip and flashlight. The problem is that the positives and negatives from the attachments are less than 10% boosts in either direction. The optimal setup on basically every gun is a vertical foregrip with the Hunter Style Muzzle Break reducing as much recoil

as possible from each weapon while only sacrificing a tiny bit of aiming & swapping speed both of which are negligible compared to the improved recoil. All of the other attachments options are really weak and there isn't any room for experimenting other than finding out that the rest of the attachments are… The choices of optics are pretty good though. Each player will have a preference for Sight picture and magnification level. The loadout you spawn with is pretty simple. Any Primary and Secondary can be equipped together. Each player spawns with two grenades and plenty of ammo. These can be refilled at ammo and health stations around the map, usually near objectives. I would again criticize the game here a bit, as there are no restrictions on the number of snipers per team, and since everyone can have the same guns and looks the same, it can sometimes be hard to tell if the person you're looking at is a friendly or enemy , there isn't any friendly fire, so you can just do a shot-check in case, but if there's an enemy in front of you and some allies in the distance, or behind a wall, directly behind them, it can lead to confusion getting you killed. Also, in these kind of games, the quality of a match decreases as the number of recon or sniper players increases. Having people jerking off to the back of the map and not making any action about the objective leads to more boring games, with less hype, and if a team is overloaded with snipers, a boring stomp as one team gets stuck in a base spawn. Lastly for gameplay, Polygon is focused on one game mode, conquest. There is

always objectives on the map to be captured and controlled, keeping the action flowing. Maps will have between 1 to 3 control points , that generate the team that owns its score. The only way for a team to win is by holding the objectives – your kills and deaths don't matter. Capturing an objective also grants your team some map control, as now you can spawn to the location rather than just your HQ. A nice thing the game does is actually updating your spawn point on the respawn screen to the closest one near your last death, so you can quickly get back into the action in that area without having to think about it. There is a second game mode available on a few maps called King of the Hill where both teams fight to control a single objective that doesn't move usually located in the centre of the map. This mode adjusts the focal points of the maps and makes them play out differently than in Conquest. Sometimes in games I feel like the maps play the same even with different objectives but Polygon nails are here The two modes are well designed and fun to play But we can't discuss game modes in full detail without looking in the maps of they are played on right listen polygon has got some of the Hands-down Best maps in a shooter for a long time each map is unique offers different gameplay opportunities and is refined and crafted to perfection. You can just feel the amount of care that has been poured into each location and each sight line. Different positions on the map give power in some way but a counterable weakness in another.
